sources.entry: Hasura - Fast, instant realtime GraphQL APIs on Postgres with fine grained access control, also trigger webhooks on database events. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Haskell/Docker/K8S
Hasura | Instant GraphQL and REST APIs on your databases

summary.one_liner: Hasura GraphQL Engine is an open source server that exposes databases (mainly PostgreSQL) through an instant, secure GraphQL API endpoint.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the Hasura engine as a project that provides access to data through a single, composable, secure API endpoint. It covers two generations: Hasura V3, which powers Hasura DDN and supports PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse and MS SQL Server via Data Connectors, with custom business logic written in TypeScript, Python or Go Connector SDKs; and Hasura V2, described as the current stable version, documented in the v2 folder. The repository is a large monorepo, and the README gives sparse-checkout instructions to fetch only the v3 folder. Support is through documentation, Discord and GitHub issues. The README itself does not document install steps for V2 or V3 beyond the clone instructions. The listing summaries describe realtime GraphQL, fine-grained access control and webhooks on database events, but the README excerpt does not expand on those features.
use_cases: instant GraphQL API over a PostgreSQL database
single secure API endpoint for application data
connecting MongoDB or MS SQL Server to a GraphQL API
writing custom business logic for a data API in TypeScript, Python or Go
building modern apps with a backend generated from existing databases
how_to_run: git clone --depth 1 (shallow clone of the full monorepo)
git checkout @ (checks out only the v3 engine code)
notable: Hasura V3 engine powers Hasura DDN and supports multiple databases through Data Connectors
Data Connectors are available as open source under Apache License 2.0
Monorepo with sparse-checkout guidance to fetch only the v3 folder
Connector SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Go to add custom logic
caveats: Monorepo is large with a long git history, so cloning is slow and uses a lot of disk space without shallow or sparse checkout
README does not give concrete install or run commands for the engine itself
The Getting Started path points to Hasura DDN, a hosted-oriented product whose setup the README does not detail
